name: Pinecone
model: Indexes split into namespaces of records (dense or sparse vector, id, metadata); filtered, hybrid and full-text search via API
engine_note: Serverless: vectors in immutable 'slabs' on object storage, recent writes in a memtable; index method chosen by slab size; internals not published
consistency: Writes are durable once logged and acked (200 OK). Per-record operations, no transactions. Officially eventually consistent: 'a slight delay' before new or changed records show in queries; log sequence numbers let you check freshness.
scaling: Serverless: storage on object storage and compute scale separately and automatically; namespaces isolate tenants; dedicated read nodes for steady heavy query load. Pod-based indexes being retired.
version_note: Latest release note: namespace aliases (2026-09-29). API is date-versioned (latest stable 2026-07). Go SDK v7.0.0 (2026-09-28) removed pod-based index creation.
reach: Reach for it when you want a hosted vector search with zero operations and pay per use, and you are fine with data living in a vendor service.
avoid: Avoid when you need self-hosting, read-your-writes guarantees, transactions with your other data, or predictable cost at very high query volume.
escape: It removes all vector index operations and scaling work, at the price of a separate managed service.
chat: Message embeddings with one namespace per user, queried by the retrieval step of the chat.
notes: Quotes: 'Pinecone is eventually consistent, so there can be a slight delay before new or changed records are visible to queries.' (check-data-freshness). Architecture page: data 'stored in highly efficient, distributed object storage' as 'immutable files called slabs'; write is logged and then the API 'immediately returns a 200 OK response, guaranteeing that your write is durable'; 'all read operations check the memtable first, so you can immediately search data that you've just written'. The two pages pull in different directions (memtable read vs official eventual consistency); the row follows the explicit 'eventually consistent' statement. Release notes 2026-09-15: pod-to-serverless migration expanded to 'up to 500 million records'. Dedicated read nodes and BYOC named from Pinecone docs and pricing, not quoted this session: unconfirmed detail. No Jepsen analysis.
